vulnerability.title: Jenkins treats backslash-prefixed redirect targets as safe, allowing open redirect

fixed_releases.verified_content: The 2.500 release commit cb753134 has 923cdbc1 as its only parent, and the SECURITY-3501 fix 4a9a3ecd is the parent of 923cdbc1 (merge-base --is-ancestor exits 0). In the 2.500 tree Util.isSafeToRedirectTo rejects any leading backslash and normalises backslashes before the // check, and the new Security3501Test asserts that userContent?path= backslash variants stay on the local userContent/ URL. The CNA record also lists LTS 2.492.2 as unaffected; that backport was not fetched or asserted.

fix_commits.branch: 2.492.x LTS release commit (backport not fetched, ancestry not asserted)

severity.numeric_level_rationale: NVD publishes a single CVSS 3.1 metric, 4.3 MEDIUM, from the Secondary source (CISA-ADP); there is no Primary metric. OSV/GHSA repeats the same 4.3 vector and records MODERATE. The CNA container has no CVSS metric. Every published severity level is MEDIUM, so the level is consistent and the score is not averaged.

vulnerability.category_l2: Redirect targets beginning with a backslash pass isSafeToRedirectTo and are sent to the client, which browsers interpret as a scheme-relative URL

description: Jenkins guards redirects with Util.isSafeToRedirectTo, which at 2.441 is !isAbsoluteUri(uri) && !uri.startsWith("//"). isAbsoluteUri only rejects a value whose ':' precedes '#', '?' or '/', so a target such as \example.org or \\example.org contains no colon and no leading "//" and is classified as safe. DirectoryBrowserSupport.serveFile uses that predicate on the pattern/path request parameter and calls sendRedirect2 with the accepted value (lines 208-209); AuthenticationSuccessHandler and ParametersDefinitionProperty apply the same predicate to their redirect targets. Browsers normalise backslashes to forward slashes for special schemes, so a redirect to \\example.org sends the user to https://example.org: the helper meant to block scheme-relative redirects lets a phishing target through. The 2.500 fix 4a9a3ecd rejects any leading backslash and normalises backslashes before the // check, and the new Security3501Test drives userContent?path= with five backslash variants and asserts the Location stays on the local userContent/ URL.

critical_operation.description: The predicate rejects absolute URIs and values starting with "//" but accepts any value starting with a backslash. Since isAbsoluteUri only treats a ':' before '#', '?' or '/' as absolute, \example.org and \\example.org pass. Callers use the accepted value for sendRedirect, so the browser resolves it as a scheme-relative URL to an external host.

entry_point.description: Example HTTP GET of /userContent?path=\\example.org (URL-encoded %5C%5Cexample.org); DirectoryBrowserSupport.serveFile passes the parameter to isSafeToRedirectTo and then sendRedirect2.

source_crosscheck.notes: The CNA, NVD, OSV and the GitHub advisory agree on the mechanism (backslash-prefixed redirect targets are treated as safe) and on the fixed releases (2.500 weekly, 2.492.2 LTS). NVD publishes no Primary metric; its only metric is the CISA-ADP Secondary 4.3 MEDIUM, which OSV/GHSA repeats, and the CNA has no metric, so all published levels are MEDIUM. CWE-601 is recorded by NVD's Secondary source and by GHSA; the CNA lists none. The GHSA ECOSYSTEM range introduced=2.493 conflicts with the CNA text and the OSV GIT range (introduced 0); this dataset follows the CNA and GIT range and records the conflict. This root cause is distinct from the previously promoted jenkins entries: CVE-2024-23897 (CLI arbitrary file read), CVE-2024-23898 (CLI WebSocket hijacking), CVE-2024-43045 (My Views permission check), CVE-2025-27622 (agent config.xml redaction) and the sibling CVE-2025-27623 (view config.xml redaction); it is a URL-safety predicate in hudson.Util.

independent_corrections_accepted: The reviewer confirmed every claimed field and supplied the exact call sites: DirectoryBrowserSupport.serveFile 205-209, AuthenticationSuccessHandler.determineTargetUrl 42-56 (predicate call at 52) and ParametersDefinitionProperty line 180.

Reporter credit: the vendor advisory credits XBOW, a third-party firm, for SECURITY-3501 rather than CloudBees. This does not change the grade, because no independent non-reporter reproduction was found; grade A still requires one.
The reviewer noted that GitHub's REST API was rate-limited and that the GHSA fields were read through OSV's mirrored GHSA record; the values agree with the OSV data already collected.
review.duplicate_check: The reviewer checked CVE-2024-23897 (CLI '@' file read), CVE-2024-23898 (CLI WebSocket origin validation), CVE-2024-43045 (My Views permission check), CVE-2025-27622 (agent config.xml redaction) and CVE-2025-27623 (view config.xml redaction) and found no duplicate: none is a backslash open redirect in the URL-safety predicate.

limitations: Static verification only; no Jenkins instance, HTTP request or browser was run.
The redirect requires a victim to follow a crafted Jenkins URL; the attacker does not need credentials for the userContent path, but the victim must click the link (UI:R).

Browser interpretation of backslash as a path separator is what turns the accepted value into an external redirect; that behaviour is asserted by the upstream test and the advisory, not executed here.

Only one location row is recorded (Util.isSafeToRedirectTo). The call sites in DirectoryBrowserSupport, AuthenticationSuccessHandler and ParametersDefinitionProperty are recorded as the entry point unless a separate CVE covers them.
The LTS backport and the 2.492.2 branch were not fetched into the local mirror; LTS ancestry is recorded from OSV and the CNA record, not asserted locally.
The GHSA ECOSYSTEM range introduced=2.493 conflicts with the CNA and the OSV GIT range; the conflict is documented, not resolved silently.
open_questions: The full set of Jenkins features that call isSafeToRedirectTo was not enumerated beyond the three found in core; the upstream test exercises the userContent path.
Whether any caller URL-encodes or normalises backslashes before the predicate was not checked for every call site.
